episode_title: 16 - Accelerated Time to Close: What does scale have to do with it?

real_qa.q: What are the five levels of accelerated time to close process in revenue operations?
real_qa.r: Level one is baseline assessment to understand what you have and where challenges exist. Level two involves analyzing how people engage with tools, technologies, content and websites to map user journeys and buyer profiles. Level three is mapping out buyer paths with buyer personas and ICPs across the customer journey. Level four is continuous improvement and optimization by reviewing data, conversion rates, and where people drop from the funnel. Level five is scaling the depth and breadth of technology and processes, moving from simple to more complex lead gen campaigns and expanding buyer personas and tech stack capabilities.
real_qa.requete: five levels accelerated time to close Rev:Up

real_qa.q: What stresses does scaling put on revenue operations processes and technology?
real_qa.r: Scaling stress-tests all the processes you have built. With a small team everyone knows their jobs and is trained by one person, but as you add more people you need documentation and well-defined processes to avoid data silos. You stress your tools and systems from both capabilities and cost perspectives. You must consider what adding 20 salespeople will do to contract costs, who will train and enable them, and how you will hold them accountable. RevOps needs to become a strategic priority rather than an afterthought.
real_qa.requete: scaling stress revenue operations processes tech stack

real_qa.q: How many systems per ops team member indicate you need additional headcount?
real_qa.r: When an ops team is operating and administering three to four systems per person, you may need to add another headcount on the ops side because you are taxing those people to their capacity and they cannot take on more work. Constantly looking at what the existing team is doing and how many people are managing these systems is really important in this landscape.
real_qa.requete: systems per ops person headcount threshold

real_qa.q: What is the cost impact when technology investment operates at low capacity utilization?
real_qa.r: A client had a six-figure annual contract for a tool they were using at only 10% capacity. If that investment in technology is not operating at its highest efficiency, the cost to the organization is significant. This is a key way to justify adding additional ops headcount by considering the cost of not adding the person versus the cost of underutilized technology investments.
real_qa.requete: technology tool capacity utilization cost ROI

real_qa.q: How does conversion rate improvement justify adding revenue operations headcount?
real_qa.r: If your conversion rate today is 3% and adding another ops person increases it to 4% or 5%, that is significant revenue moved down the pipeline to close. You have paid for that person already just through that one small change. Optimizing handoffs between teams and ensuring leads receive the right content at the right buying stage improves conversion efficiency and reduces time salespeople spend educating prospects who are already educated by marketing.
real_qa.requete: conversion rate optimization revenue ops headcount ROI

real_qa.q: Why do many organizations overlook revenue operations as a strategic priority when scaling?
real_qa.r: Many leaders focus on fundraising and how to deploy funds across sales, marketing, and channel expansion, but few have dedicated RevOps ownership. Some organizations may have a marketing technology owner, a Salesforce administrator, or a finance person trying to cover RevOps, but there is not enough bandwidth or strategic attention. The perception is often that RevOps is good enough or running adequately, but databases become outdated, processes are not followed, and RevOps does not receive the attention it needs as the company scales.
real_qa.requete: revenue operations RevOps strategic priority scaling

guest.bio_context: Jen Kors is co-host of Rev:Up Live alongside David Knorr and specializes in accelerated time to close processes and revenue operations strategy. She leads the team's focus on scalability, process optimization, and the stress-testing of organizational capabilities when companies scale. Jen has worked extensively with clients on baseline assessments, data analysis, buyer journey mapping, and the implementation of RevOps functions across growing organizations.
